rule: R-ENF-01 / the exemplar is held to the standard it defines
note: Standards the model report is outstanding on. It may only ever SHORTEN: a new standard is either MET by the exemplar or the entry is added here deliberately, in the commit that adopts it. [05-Sep-2026] THE LIST GREW FROM ONE TO EIGHT AND SEVEN OF THE SEVEN WERE ALWAYS THERE. This gate matched only a list item equal to a ticker, so it was blind to a group stored as a DICT keyed by ticker (how terminal_outstanding and lens_vocabulary_outstanding store theirs), a list of FILE PATHS, and a dict keyed by path. THE GATE WHOSE WHOLE PURPOSE IS TO NOTICE THE EXEMPLAR ACQUIRING DEBT COULD NOT SEE FOUR FIFTHS OF IT — and the rule's own adoption note records the exemplar as outstanding on EIGHT ratchets, which is what this now reports, so it has been under-reporting since the day it shipped. One of the eight IS new and is added deliberately in the commit that adopts it, exactly as this rule requires.

reasons.ADNOCLS:rebuild_outstanding.json:outstan: ADDED DELIBERATELY IN THE COMMIT THAT ADOPTS [R-REBUILD-01], which is what that gate asks for. The rule binds on a study whose committed answer HAS MOVED since its delivered edition; the exemplar has not been rebuilt since the rule exists, so it has no route to record and there is nothing for it to meet. THE DEBT IS NOT A CONSTRUCTION A NEW STUDY WOULD INHERIT — a study written by opening the model report beside it copies its sections, its sheets and its constructions, and "carries no rebuild ledger because it has not been rebuilt" is not one of those; it is a fact about history rather than a property of the document. The entry comes off the moment the exemplar is re-issued, at which point it owes a ledger like any other rebuilt study.
reasons.ADCB:coverage_outstanding.json:entries: NOT A DEBT THE EXEMPLAR OWES AND RECORDED SO RATHER THAN DROPPED. ADCB is a lens PATTERN reference (the bank row), not a study in this repository, so it appears on the coverage list for the same reason every uncovered name does — a published fair value with no study directory. Its presence is a coverage fact, not a standard the reference set fails. It became visible on 05-Sep-2026 when this gate learned to read a ratchet stored as a dict.
reasons.ALPHADHABI:coverage_outstanding.json:ent: As ADCB above — the holdco pattern reference, not a study here.
reasons.ADNOCLS:band_outstanding.json:documents: THE EXEMPLAR PUBLISHES THE RETIRED SKILL VERDICT: "the three-month distributions scored +2.95% better than a random-walk benchmark anchored on the same cost of carry", built at docx_adnocls.py:2348 from BT3[skill_norm]. [R-CAL-03] retires that outright from every public surface and a delivered study is one. ADDED DELIBERATELY IN THE COMMIT THAT WIDENS THE PATTERNS, which is what the exemplar rule asks for: the debt is recorded as GROWING rather than the choice being made silently. THIS IS THE WORST PLACE FOR IT — a new study is written by opening this document, so the sentence propagates looking exactly like the house standard, and it already has: SWDY and ADNOCDRILL carry the same claim in their own words. The fix is one clause in one builder and a rebuild of the document and its PDF; it is a re-issue of the model report and is not taken in the same pass that found it.
reasons.ADNOCLS:edition_outstanding.json:outstan: became visible on 05-Sep-2026 when this gate learned to read a ratchet keyed by DOCUMENT PATH rather than by ticker. The entry itself is not new.
reasons.ADNOCLS:lens_vocabulary_outstanding.json: became visible on 05-Sep-2026 when this gate learned to read a ratchet stored as a DICT keyed by ticker. The entry itself is not new.
reasons.ADNOCLS:terminal_outstanding.json:signat: became visible on 05-Sep-2026 when this gate learned to read a ratchet stored as a DICT keyed by ticker. The entry itself is not new and is the substantive one: the exemplar builds its terminal on the retired reinvestment identity, implied cycle 50.0 years against 1/g of 50.0, charging 18.1% of terminal profit, and it is the ONE study in the book whose terminal sits BELOW its own floor at -7.5%. Every study written by opening it inherits that construction.
reasons.ADCB:no_record_outstanding.json:no_recor: NOT A DEBT THE EXEMPLAR OWES, AND ADDED ONE COMMIT LATE — WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING. [R-GAP-01]'s gate was re-pointed on 06-09-2026 from the engine/*_study glob to the 90 delivered studies, and the new no_record_dir list was seeded with every covered name that commits no record directory. ADCB is a lens PATTERN reference, not a study in this repository, so it lands there for exactly the reason the coverage entry above names: a published fair value with no study directory. Its presence is a POPULATION fact, not a construction a new study would inherit by opening the model report beside it — which is the harm this rule exists to stop. WHAT WENT WRONG PROCEDURALLY IS THE POINT: [R-ENF-01 EXTENDED 04-Sep-2026] says a new standard is either MET by the exemplar or CONSCIOUSLY ADDED here IN THE COMMIT THAT ADOPTS IT, and this entry was added in the NEXT one. The seeding commit ran the gates it judged affected — valuation gap, lens design, prose figures, artefact currency, workbook values — and check_exemplar_debt was not among them, so a CI-wired gate went red and the desk that made the change did not know. It was found by an outside gate-runner asked to audit the re-point, which is the argument for running the whole set rather than the affected-looking subset [R-ENF-04]: the gate you do not think to run is the one that was watching. [MOVED 06-09-2026, SAME DAY] the no-record set left gap_outstanding.json for a SHARED ratchet before the other ten gates could each seed a copy of it, so this entry follows the fact rather than the file. The key is the ratchet's own path, which is why a move reads as a change here rather than as nothing — the entries are keyed EXEMPLAR:ratchet:list exactly so a name travelling between lists cannot pass silently.
